definition: A cultivated recognition that keeps the impermanent character of conditioned experience in view.
notes: Use this record for the three-marks practice family when impermanence is cultivated as a steady recognition rather than treated as a mere abstract doctrine. The English follows the sanna record's default: recognition, not perception. Perception is discouraged here because readers take a perception to be a thing in its own right, something held and lasting, whereas saññā is the act of knowing the thing again -- re-cognizing it -- which is exactly the activity this practice trains. In the canonical recognition lists it belongs to the insight-training sequence and should stay linked to the broader progression toward seeing dissatisfaction and not-self.

example_phrases.notes: Listed among the cultivated recognitions used for insight and release.
